chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran who said:
I asked him about what the hunting dog trained for hunting holds back.

And it is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And what you have learned of the hunting beasts, teaching them as Allah has taught you, so eat from what they catch for you and mention the name of Allah over it.'
He said: 'There is no harm in eating from what the dog holds back, from what the dog has not eaten from it; but if the dog eats from it before you catch it, then do not eat from it.'
He said: And I asked him about the prey of the cheetah, which is trained for hunting, so he said: 'If you catch it alive, slaughter it and eat it; and if it kills it, do not eat from it.'

key_terms.الْكَلْبُ الْمُعَلَّمُ لِلصَّيْدِ: The hunting dog trained for hunting

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat caught by a trained hunting dog or cheetah if the animal has eaten from it?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Samaanah ibn Mihran from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), elucidates the conditions for the permissibility of game caught by trained beasts of prey, distinguishing between consumption by the animal and the method of slaughter. It establishes that if the dog eats from the prey before the owner arrives, the meat becomes impure, whereas for the cheetah, the owner must perform the ritual slaughter if the prey is alive, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on proper *dhikr* and physical purity in hunting.
